newsitem.title: USA: USDA seen cutting US soy ending stocks projection.
newsitem.headline: USDA seen cutting US soy ending stocks projection.

text.p: A further cut in projected U.S. soybean ending stocks for 1996/97 (September/August) may be made next week by the U.S. Department of Agriculture in its monthly Supply/Demand Report, analysts said.

"They (USDA) are still a little shy on exports and crush although the probability of them making big changes is modest. They really tightened it up good last month," said Chicago-based analyst Jerry Gidel of Dean Witter.
Last month USDA cut its soybean ending stocks estimate to 155 million bushels from 180 million a month earlier.
The USDA report will be released on Wednesday.
Gidel said he was projecting ending stocks at 125 million bushels, with his crush total 20 million bushels above USDA's current figure and exports 10 million bushels stronger.
He did not expect USDA to make that substantial a cut and believed its total was more likely to be around 140 million.
"Anything you take off 155 million is going to be bullish," Gidel said.
Chicago analyst Mickey Luth of the LaiFa Group said the crush would probably be raised by at least 10 million bushels and exports could also possibly be raised on the USDA report.
"They cannot help but raise the crush. We are crushing at a phenomenal rate to meet European demand. They could raise the exports too but that one is not as pressing as the crush," he said.
Analysts said there was a possibility that USDA would raise its soybean production estimates for Brazil and Argentina with many higher private estimates circulating.

A recent report from the U.S. agricultural attache in Sao Paulo, however, continued to indicate a production outlook of around 26 million tonnes for Brazil, little changed from USDA's January projection of 25.90 million.
The attache report, however, noted some private analysts' forecasts for soy output in excess of 27 million tonnes.

"I think that USDA, in terms of combined production could be two million low. The Argentine crop could be up to 14 million, the Brazilian crop at least 27 million," said Everen Securities analyst Joel Karlin.
USDA's current estimate for Argentina is 12.65 million.
Karlin said, however, USDA may wait until next month before hiking its South American soybean estimates.
"They might not do it yet. They might wait until next month when the flowering period is completely over," he said.
